title: [epic] User roles & auth hardening
description: Follow-up to the review of PR #5 (add user roles): https://github.com/DomasB/polito-log/pull/5. Blocking bugs: B1, UserRole is persisted by enum name (DEFAULT) while the migration writes values (default), which raises LookupError on load, so nobody can log in after deploy. B2, Alembic has no baseline and create_all still runs, so deploys fail on fresh and existing DBs. Security: the first user to verify a magic link becomes admin (privilege escalation). Pre-existing auth weaknesses S2-S7 filed as separate children. Agreed fix order: B1 -> B2 -> S1 -> S2 -> S3 -> S4-S7.
design: Admins are bootstrapped via a CLI command, never by first-user-admin. role is the single source of privilege, read from the DB on each request, never from the JWT. Implement on a fresh branch from main, carrying over the useful parts of PR #5 (enum, Alembic scaffolding, docs) in fixed form; close PR #5 as superseded once task 1/2 ships. Running migrations via Railway preDeployCommand depends on polito-log-cf2 (Railway ignores railway.json and builds with Railpack, so PR #5's CMD ./start.sh would never run in prod).
acceptance_criteria: All 11 children closed. Deploys succeed on fresh and existing DBs with migrations run in preDeploy. Login works for every role. No request path can grant privilege. Admins are created only via the CLI, with audit rows. PR #5 closed as superseded.

title: Smart Search (Kernel + Plugins)
description:
Unified, tokenized, URL-synced search for political statements. Single input field handles free text and structured filters (e.g. status:verified), rendering committed filters as editable chips.

ARCHITECTURE — Kernel + Plugins model. The Kernel runs the core loop (input -> parse -> state -> render) and knows how to process tokens, not what they mean. Plugins are self-contained modules in four categories:
- Filter plugins ('what'): own keys like status/date; parse, validate, suggest values, render tokens.
- Operator plugins ('how'): define comparisons (:, =, !=, >, <, ~).
- Action plugins ('do'): run commands instead of filtering (e.g. > save, > export).
- Global-suggestion plugins ('discover'): suggestions for empty/unmatched input (recent searches, saved views).
A central Registry indexes plugins by key/symbol/trigger; the Parser delegates classification to it.

PROGRESSION — encoded via priority: P1 = MVP (kernel + essentials), P2 = quick wins, P3 = advanced, P4 = out-there. Each child task is labeled frontend / backend / fullstack. Already-implemented foundation work is tracked as closed tasks.

Design reference (kept in repo): frontend/src/components/search/ARCHITECTURE.md, PLUGINS.md, PLAN.md.
design: Architecture/contracts live in frontend/src/components/search/{ARCHITECTURE,PLUGINS}.md; UX tiers in PLAN.md. Kernel+Plugins: core loop (input->parse->state->render) + plugins (filter/operator/action/global-suggestion) indexed by a Registry. Phases encoded via priority P1(MVP)->P4(out-there).

title: Magic links: hash at rest, atomic consume, invalidate siblings
description:
S7a: magic-link tokens are stored in plaintext, consume is check-then-update (race allows double use), and older outstanding links stay valid. Files: backend/app/models/magic_link.py, backend/app/repositories/magic_link.py, backend/app/services/auth.py, migration.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Request a magic link; inspect the magic_links table: the token is stored in plaintext.
2. Request two links for the same email: both remain valid after one is used.
3. Fire two concurrent POSTs to verify with the same token: both can pass the is_used check before either marks it used, yielding two sessions.
acceptance_criteria: SHA-256 of the token stored, never plaintext. Consume is a single UPDATE ... WHERE is_used=false AND expires_at>now() RETURNING. Other outstanding links for the same email are invalidated on consume. Concurrency test proves single use.
